abstract: Mercer's 11th annual Global Talent Trends survey (nearly 12,000 executives, HR leaders, investors, and employees worldwide, fielded September-October 2025) on how AI is reshaping workforce planning. Headline: most executives expect substantial redeployment and reskilling rather than outright elimination, while employee job-loss concern has risen sharply.
keyFindings: 65% of executives expect 11%-30% of their workforce to be redeployed or reskilled due to AI over the next two years.
Employee concern about job loss due to AI surged from 28% in 2024 to 40% in 2026.
98% of executives are planning organizational design changes over the next two years.
Investors say companies combining human and AI capabilities gain a competitive advantage.
methodology: Global survey of nearly 12,000 C-suite executives, HR leaders, employees, and investors across 16 geographies and 16 industries, conducted September-October 2025; released February 2026. 11th year of the series.
qualifiers: Redeployment/reskilling expectations are not job-loss projections - classified as a neutral overlay on the displacement chart. Global sample, not US-specific. Executive expectations, not realized outcomes.
